meta.title: When you need tmux from a phone — 6 real scenarios
meta.description: Six real reasons to reach tmux from a phone: unattended agents, on-call triage, commutes, travelling without a laptop, long jobs and a machine behind NAT.

hero.title: The work doesn't stop when you leave the desk.
hero.lead: Six situations mtmux was built around. If none of them look like your week, you probably don't need it.

unattendedAgents.title: A 40-minute refactor you didn't watch
unattendedAgents.body1: <post>Agents don't fail loudly</post>. They finish quietly, or wait forever on a permission dialog you'd have answered in a second.
unattendedAgents.body2: So look at the pane. Open the session on your phone, read what the agent actually printed, and tap y — it is the same pty your laptop was attached to, so nothing is lost in translation.

terminal.title: iphone — work:1
terminal.question: Apply patch to migrations/0042.sql?
terminal.options: ❯ 1. Yes    2. No, tell Claude what to change

onCall.title: Triage before you find a laptop
onCall.body1: The first five minutes of an incident are k9s, logs and one restart. That fits on a phone.
onCall.body2: Your jump-host session is already open, with the dashboards you left running. No key on the phone, no VPN to negotiate at 2am.

commuting.title: Twenty minutes of real progress
commuting.body1: Read the diff the agent produced, kick off the next task, watch a test run, fix a config line — <post>all of it from a phone</post>.
commuting.body2: The client reconnects on its own, so going through a tunnel costs you a moment rather than the session.

travellingLight.title: Tablet, keyboard, no laptop
travellingLight.body1: A tablet keeps real splits, and a Bluetooth keyboard passes chords straight through — prefix key included.
travellingLight.body2: Your workstation does the compiling; the tablet is a very good terminal for it.

longJobs.title: Training runs and migrations
longJobs.body1: A six-hour job mostly needs one thing from you: an occasional glance to confirm it is still moving.
longJobs.body2: Start it in tmux as you already would, and check the pane from wherever you are. mtmux doesn't wrap the command or watch its exit code — it just shows you the pane.

behindNat.title: A machine you can't route to
behindNat.body1: A workstation at home, a box on a corporate network, a Pi behind carrier-grade NAT. There is no port to forward, and often no authority to forward one.
behindNat.body2: mtmux dials out, so reachability is not your problem to solve. If you'd rather it never left the building, mtmux start --local serves the LAN and contacts nothing.

cta.title: Try it on today's session.
cta.description: Nothing to migrate and nothing to configure. If it isn't useful in a day, uninstall it — your tmux sessions never noticed it was there.
